general_conventions: M1 = method mark; a later A1 that depends on it cannot be scored without it; in 'show that' items the final A mark is often A0 (the given value earns nothing on its own).
C1 = compensatory method mark, awarded automatically if the final answer is correct; A1 = accuracy mark for the final value; B1 = independent mark for a stated fact or step.

ECF (error carried forward): later numerical parts can earn full credit if consistent with an earlier wrong answer; ECF is allowed after arithmetic (AE), transcription (TE) and power-of-ten (POT) errors but not after wrong physics / wrong equation (XP).
POT: power-of-ten slip (usually an SI-prefix conversion) loses the mark where it occurs, then ECF applies.

SF: giving more significant figures than justified is not penalised; too few is dealt with in individual guidance (often 1 SF is allowed where stated); the SF penalty is applied only once in the paper unless a question explicitly demands a given number of SF.
XP: use of an incorrect equation counts as wrong physics even if it happens to give the right number.
CON: a contradiction within the same response cancels the mark; BOD = benefit of doubt; ^ marks an omission (not wrong but incomplete).

Notation: '/' separates alternatives; Reject/Not = not creditworthy; Ignore = irrelevant extra; Allow = acceptable; words in brackets are not essential; underlined words must be present; AW = alternative wording; ORA = or reverse argument.
General rule for Section B: substitution into an equation may be made with any quantity as subject unless the guidance says otherwise.
Significant figures: if data are given to 2 SF allow answers to 2 or more SF; fewer than 2 SF penalised once only in the whole paper unless guidance says otherwise.
B marks are independent; M marks must be seen and A marks depend on them; C marks can be credited implicitly from correct later working.
MCQ: two responses for a single-answer question score zero; contradictory responses score zero.
NR (no response) for blank answers, unrelated comments or non-attempt marks; 0 for attempts that earn nothing (including copying out the question).

Level-of-response guidance (2025 wording): find the level by working down from the highest; position within level from 'borderline' (bottom) to 'consistently meets criteria' (top). No LoR question on this paper.

questions.context: Evaluate identification as type Z given n = 1.52 ± 1.5% and type ranges.
questions.answer: Range ≈1.497–1.543 overlaps types Y and Z, so conclusion not secure.

questions.context: What critical angle means.
questions.answer: Angle of incidence at which refraction angle is 90°.
marking_points: B1: angle of incidence for which angle of refraction is 90° (refracted ray along boundary)
pitfalls: Only saying 'angle where TIR starts' without the 90° refraction condition.

questions.subtopic: measuring critical angle with semicircular dish
questions.context: Describe accurately measuring critical angle in a semicircular liquid dish using a ray box.
questions.answer: Aim ray through curved side at centre of flat edge; vary angle until refracted ray grazes boundary; trace rays and normal; measure with protractor.
marking_points: B1: ray aimed through curved side to the middle of the straight edge
B1: move ray box/rotate dish until critical case seen
B1 × 2: any two of — dish on paper with outline/normal drawn; trace incident ray; protractor measures angle; correct critical angle identified on diagram
allow_reject_ignore: Credit from a clear diagram; ignore calculation methods.
pitfalls: Entering through the flat side; measuring angle from the surface not the normal.

questions.context: State the principle of moments.

pitfalls: Omitting 'in equilibrium' or 'about the same point'.
